primary_task: Set up AFL++ (instrumented build, seeds, multi-core primary/secondary campaign) for a C/C++ target and run and triage a fuzzing campaign.

requirements.name: AFL++ (apt package, Docker image, or source build)
requirements.evidence: Installation table: "Ubuntu/Debian repos" / "Docker (from Docker Hub)" / "From source"; `apt install afl++ lld-17` (alternatives; any one suffices)
requirements.basis: bash: install packages from the open registries (... apt from Ubuntu ...); Ubuntu apt archives are open

requirements.name: clang/LLVM or GCC with plugin dev packages
Docker (wrapper `./afl++ docker ...`)
requirements.evidence: "The examples below use `docker` mode ... Swap in `host` to run any of them against an AFL++ installed on the machine itself."
requirements.basis: lacks: a Docker daemon (docker, docker compose and container builds cannot run)

requirements.name: Docker Hub (aflplusplus/aflplusplus image)
requirements.basis: lacks: network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open

requirements.name: root / kernel tuning (afl-system-config, afl-persistent-config, reboot)
requirements.evidence: "Run after each reboot for up to 15% more executions per second"
requirements.basis: The manifest does not say whether the session has root or may change kernel settings; the step is an optional speed-up.

requirements.name: fuzz target source code and harness
requirements.basis: Supplied by the user's working directory; the manifest says nothing.

notes: Strict literal reading of the examples (every command prefixed `./afl++ docker`) would make Docker required and the verdict BLOCKED (program:docker). I took the document's own statement that `host` mode is a drop-in replacement with AFL++ installed from apt, so Docker is one alternative.
